title: Weekly briefing: the Crimean Bridge war, missiles in Poland, and Iran widens its targets
summary: The first weekly edition covers November sixteenth to twenty-third: Ukraine's strikes cut the Crimean Bridge and Russia answers with a barrage of more than a hundred missiles, three of which land in Poland; Trump meets Putin in China; a drone kills eleven in Dymer; Ukraine hits a Russian warship in Libya; the US strikes Qeshm Island as Iran hits Bahrain and Kuwait; the George Washington leaves the Middle East; and the Houthis close in on Aden.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Welcome to the ForceFinder Briefing. I'm Avery.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And I'm Cole. As always, this show is generated automatically from the open-source reporting behind the ForceFinder map. Every story has source links on the globe, so treat us as a guide, not the final word.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And there's something new this time. We're moving from a daily show to a weekly one. So this is our first weekly edition, covering Monday the sixteenth through today, Monday, November twenty-third.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And it was a big week to start with. Let's begin with the story that drove most of the others. The Crimean Bridge.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Last Monday, we told you about Ukraine's record drone raid, when Russia said it shot down more than thirteen hundred drones and the bridge was hit. That turned out to be the first of three strikes on the bridge in four days.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Overnight into Tuesday, Ukraine's General Staff says a strike destroyed a span of the bridge's road section. President Putin later said the road side had been seriously damaged.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Then on Thursday, Ukraine's Defence Ministry says Neptune missiles hit the railway section. Trains were suspended. Russia's transport ministry said no one was hurt, and traffic resumed that afternoon.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Putin promised a response that would be, quote, far more painful. And it came the next night.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Overnight into Friday, Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched more than a hundred missiles and about four hundred drones, mostly at the energy system. At least eight people were killed, six of them in Kyiv. The grid operator reported significant damage.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And some of those missiles didn't stay in Ukraine. Polish prosecutors say three Russian Kh-one-oh-one cruise missiles came down in eastern Poland, in Nowy Lipowiec, Rudnik and Molodycz.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Prime Minister Donald Tusk called it an apparent deliberate provocation. NATO called it a grave violation of Polish airspace. President Trump called it a mistake. Whether it was deliberate is still unresolved.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Speaking of Trump, he met Vladimir Putin in person on Thursday, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific summit in Shenzhen, China. It was their first face-to-face meeting in more than a year, and it lasted about forty minutes.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: The Kremlin says Ukraine dominated the conversation. But no agreement to halt the fighting was announced. And within a day, Russia had launched that massive barrage.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: The weekend was the deadliest stretch for civilians. On Sunday, a Russian drone hit a five-storey apartment block in Dymer, north of Kyiv. Police say eleven people were killed, including an eleven-year-old girl.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And in Vyshneve, just outside the capital, a drone hit a supermarket. Al Jazeera reported three killed and fifteen injured, though other reports gave lower figures. Officials put the Kyiv region's weekend toll at fourteen to fifteen, and today is a day of mourning there.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Ukraine's long-range campaign didn't let up either. Drones hit the Afipsky and Ilsky refineries in Russia's south again on Wednesday. And overnight into today, Ukraine's General Staff confirmed strikes on the Novoshakhtinsk refinery in the Rostov region, which reportedly halted operations, and on a pumping station in Tatarstan.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Plus Perm, more than fifteen hundred kilometres from Ukraine. The regional governor says an industrial facility was damaged, and independent media say it was the Lukoil refinery there.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And the most unusual strike of the week was nowhere near Ukraine. Ukraine's security service says seven naval drones, launched from a mother ship, hit the Russian corvette Merkury and a cargo ship called the Angara at Benghazi, in Libya.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Zelensky says the corvette sank. Libyan officials say it was severely damaged. Libya's eastern government has asked the United Nations to investigate.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: On the front lines, the Institute for the Study of War says both sides made small advances southwest of Druzhkivka and Dobropillia, with Ukrainian gains in and east of Dobropillia. And it reports a Russian infiltration on the edge of Kupiansk-Vuzlovyi.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Zelensky's own count for the week is striking. About two thousand seven hundred drones, fourteen hundred and sixty glide bombs, and a hundred and sixty-five missiles fired at Ukraine.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Now to the Gulf, where Iran's confrontation with the United States widened this week.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: On Tuesday, Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed a drone attack on an American radar at Isa Air Base in Bahrain. That was their third claimed attack on US sites in Bahrain in five days.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And this time, Washington hit back. A US official says American jets struck a Revolutionary Guard missile launch site on Qeshm Island, in self-defence. That's the second publicly reported US strike on that island this month.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Iran then fired at Kuwait for the first time since early September, targeting US installations at Ali Al Salem air base. Kuwait says its air defences engaged the drones, and there was no damage.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And on Saturday came the most serious hit on Bahrain yet. Bahrain says an Iranian strike set a civilian industrial site on fire and injured two people. Smoke was seen over Sitra Island, home to a refinery. The Guards claimed they destroyed two American Patriot radars, which hasn't been confirmed.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Bahrain is now demanding compensation and action from the UN Security Council.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: At sea, the tanker war continues. On Sunday, the Guards said two more tankers hit mines north of Ghanem Island, east of the strait. They also claimed to have shot down an American drone. Neither claim has been independently confirmed.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And there's talk of Iran trying to break the American blockade outright, with a convoy of more than fourteen loaded tankers. President Trump said any such tankers would end up, quote, at the bottom of the sea. Iran's foreign ministry called the convoy reports speculation.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Which brings us to the ships. Last week we had three American carriers in the region. That lasted only a few days.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: USNI News reported on Wednesday that the George Washington left the Middle East after three months and is now in the Seventh Fleet area, back toward the Pacific. So the Theodore Roosevelt did relieve it, and the region is back to two carriers, the Roosevelt and the George H. W. Bush.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: We've moved the George Washington to an estimated position in the Indian Ocean. And one note on the Makin Island amphibious group. This week's fleet tracker shows one of its ships, the Anchorage, at Yokosuka, but we couldn't confirm where Makin Island itself is, so its marker stays at its last reported position.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Now Yemen, where the Houthis kept up their push toward Aden. Reuters reported them within about eighty kilometres of the city by Tuesday, fighting at Tur al-Bahah, one of the main approaches, after cutting a government supply route along the coast.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: We've updated that Houthi area on the map's armed-groups layer, along the Bab el-Mandeb coast. It's still marked contested.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Saudi Arabia hit back hard. The Saudi-led coalition says it struck sixty Houthi targets on Tuesday, including tunnels used for ballistic missiles. The Houthi-run health ministry says at least seventeen people were killed, which can't be verified. On Friday, the coalition struck Hodeidah port, saying it was going after weapons smuggling.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And the missiles kept coming the other way. Two aimed at Jazan on Friday, three at Riyadh on Saturday. All intercepted, according to the coalition. The Houthis are now threatening Saudi Red Sea ports and power plants.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: In Gaza, the strikes continue despite the ceasefire. Six people were killed in central Gaza on Saturday, according to the civil defence agency. And today, at least five more, including a worker for the UN agency for Palestinian refugees.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: In Lebanon, Israel says it struck a Hezbollah missile production and storage site in the east on Thursday, its second strike there in a week. And in Sudan, Amnesty International called for a war crimes investigation into drone strikes on the city of El Obeid by the Rapid Support Forces.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: A quick look at the numbers. The strike archive on the site added twenty-one entries this week, and now holds a hundred and sixty-three strikes going back to early October. You can chart them and download them from the Strike data section.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: So, what to watch in the coming week. Whether NATO does anything more about the missiles in Poland. Whether Iran actually tries to run the blockade with that tanker convoy, and how Washington responds. Repairs to the Crimean Bridge, and Russia's next move. And whether the Houthis reach the outskirts of Aden.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: That's the briefing. Thanks for listening, and we'll see you next week.
